belief: My worth depends on how I look.
origins: Constant evaluation of faces and bodies, by media, peers, and ourselves, can make appearance the basis of identity. Aging and change then threaten our worth itself.
teaches: “You made him a little lower than the angels; You crowned him with glory and honor.” “God created man in His own image.” “Charm is deceptive and beauty is fleeting, but a woman who fears the LORD is to be praised” (Proverbs 31:30). Worth is established by God’s creation and love, not by looks. Appearance is one small part of a person.
self_statements: If I look bad, I am worthless.
I need to look good to matter.
I cannot go out without makeup.
errors: Believing I am either attractive and valuable or not.
Predicting that aging will ruin my worth.
Feeling bad about my looks and concluding I am worthless.
questions: What part of my worth do I tie to my looks?
What do I admire in others besides their looks?
What happens when I skip checking the mirror?
What did God declare about humanity in Genesis?
What could I do to care for myself without obsession?
What matters most to me at the end of life?
truth: My worth rests in God’s creation, love, and calling, not in my looks. I can care for myself with gratitude and move my attention to what lasts.
hw_truths: I am crowned with glory and honor.
I am made in God’s image.
God loves me as I am.
I can care for myself kindly.
log: Each week, note one thing you did that had nothing to do with appearance.
actions: Count how often you check the mirror.
Invest in a skill or kindness.
prayer: Lord, I have tied my worth to my looks. Free me, teach me to see myself as You do, and help me invest in what lasts. Amen.
